title: Canonical scalar tensor models compatible with open inverse image
statement: There exist presentations $m$ of the existing ordinary unbounded constant-coefficient pro-etale derived tensor/scalar adjunctions and normalized tensor comparison choices $c$ [def-sp-open-scalar-tensor-data], such that scalar projection $K\otimes_A^L\operatorname{Res}(B)\to\operatorname{Res}(S_TK)$ is invertible for every finite commutative $A,B$, coefficient map $A\to B$, scheme $T$, and arbitrary derived $K$. Moreover, for every open immersion $j:U\to X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and arbitrary $F,Q\in D(X,A)$, the inverse scalar/inverse-image comparison $\lambda^{-1}$ is tensor compatible: writing $t_T$ for scalar tensorators and $a_A,a_B$ for inverse-image tensorators, $(\lambda_F^{-1}\otimes\lambda_Q^{-1});a_B^{-1};j_B^{-1}(t_X^{-1})=t_U^{-1};S_U(a_A^{-1});\lambda_{F\otimes Q}^{-1}$. The choices include strong monoidal open inverse image with tensorator precisely the canonical restriction tensor comparison. No boundedness or flatness of the coefficient map is assumed.

proof.text: Choose the canonical closed symmetric monoidal derived structures and their representative coherence, then the normalized scalar adjunction pairs and scalar tensor comparisons. The choice uses proved constructions, not an arbitrary witness of mere existence.

Descend the ordinary restriction tensor and unit comparisons on flat-term K-flat representatives. Their pure-tensor associativity and unit diagrams give the strong monoidal structure with exactly the prescribed restriction tensorator. The two ringed-topos factorizations have the same balanced representative map, giving the displayed inverse tensor equation.
The scalar projection adjunct on a K-flat representative is x tensor b mapped to b tensor x, so it is the usual scalar-extension identification and is invertible. Descend to all derived objects.
